newsitem.title: USA: Mass. sees shipyard plan creating up to 2,000 jobs.
newsitem.headline: Mass. sees shipyard plan creating up to 2,000 jobs.

text.p: Mass. Gov. William Weld said on Thursday that he hoped President Bill Clinton this weekend will approve plans to modernize the Quincy Shipyard, which could create as many as 2,000 jobs on the South Shore.

The governor said fellow Republicans U.S. House Speaker Newt Gingrich and Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott told him bills authorizing the U.S. Maritime Administration to provide loan guarantees are part of the Omnibus Appropriations Bill.
"Restoring the shipyard brings back the historic tradition of shipbuilding in Quincy, and will also create thousands of new jobs for the South Shore," Weld said, in prepared remarks.
The shipyard will be restored by Massachusetts Heavy Industries, which will buy the Fore River Shipyard from the Massachusetts Water Resource Authority for $10 million.
The Maritime Administration will provide $42 million in loan guarantees to help secure funding for the modernization.

Once this phase is completed, the company plans to begin building six double-hull cargo carriers, which will require the Maritime agency to provide $200 million of loan guarantees. Each of the six contracts is worth $42 million to $50 million.
